output.summary: Deterministic verdict: PASS (analysis-result.json#/policy_verdict). Run validity VALID; analysis coverage COMPLETE. Both evaluated windows PASS: reference (epoch 1704067200000–1704067320000, latency p95 50ms) and workload-01 (epoch 1704067320000–1704067800000, latency p95 100ms) both satisfy the latency policy observed <= 200ms and the resource SLA checks (system-cpu-work 0.15 and system-db-work 0.015, both not > 0.9). Internally, the analysis reported one candidate anomaly (response_time_p95 step from a flat 50ms reference to a flat 100ms in workload-01, episode 1704067500000–1704067800000, max_abs_delta 50ms) and two candidate associations (downstream in_flight_requests and generator active_threads vs p95 latency; raw/partial rho ~0.998, best-lag rho ~0.999 at -1000ms). Those candidates have uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, their headline significance selection is UNAVAILABLE (OBSERVATION_COUNT_UNSUPPORTED), and clock alignment is not verified by core, so they remain hypotheses and do not change the PASS verdict.

hypotheses.observation: In workload-01, p95 latency is 100ms versus 50ms in the reference window (latency policy still PASS at threshold 200ms), and in the same window generator active_threads rose to mean ~4.87 / median 6 from ~3 in reference, while dependency in_flight_requests rose to mean ~4.15 / median 5.28 from ~2.28 in reference; the response anomaly episode starts at epoch 1704067500000 with max_abs_delta 50ms.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The response-time step could reflect a concurrency- or workload-profile change (more generator threads and more downstream in-flight work in the same period) rather than a service regression, but that is a hypothesis; the evidence does not establish which side drove the change.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the generator thread configuration and downstream service telemetry/logs around epoch 1704067500000, and rerun with an explicitly documented step profile so the intended concurrency change is recorded.

hypotheses.observation: association-08 (downstream-wait vs response_time_p95) and association-09 (generator-threads vs response_time_p95) are CANDIDATE with identical lag profiles, best_lag_ms -1000, best_lag_rho 0.999342586275, raw_rho/partial_rho 0.998274154046, reasons CONSTANT_CONTROL and CLOCK_ALIGNMENT_UNKNOWN, uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED; their headline selections are UNAVAILABLE with reason OBSERVATION_COUNT_UNSUPPORTED.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The two candidate series have byte-identical lag profiles and rho values, so they may be mirroring the same underlying signal or a metadata coupling rather than two independent causes; and because clock alignment is not verified by core, the -1000ms best lag cannot support a lead/lag ordering.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock alignment across generator, service, dependency, and telemetry first; then extend the window or rerun to obtain enough observations for the family-corrected headline test, and confirm that downstream-wait and generator-threads are independently collected signals.

hypotheses.observation: target_rate and generator request_starts are constant 60 req/s in both windows (min=mean=max=60); associations 01–07 are INSUFFICIENT_DATA with reasons NO_RANK_VARIATION, NO_RESIDUAL_VARIATION, CONSTANT_CONTROL, CLOCK_ALIGNMENT_UNKNOWN, LAG_NOT_EVALUABLE, RESOURCE_DELTA_BELOW_MINIMUM, and the control target-request-rate was requested but dropped (controls_used empty).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: With a constant load control and flat resource series, correlation cannot be estimated; this is a coverage limitation of the analysis, not proof that resources are stable or that no relationship exists.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun with a stepped or ramped load profile so the control and resource series have rank variation, and verify clocks so lag evaluation is possible before drawing any association conclusions.

hypotheses.observation: cpu-service-quota quota_fraction is constant 1.0 (min=mean=max=1) in both windows while system-cpu-work is 0.15 and system-db-work is 0.015; the resource SLA checks for cpu-work and db-work PASS because 0.15 and 0.015 are not > 0.9.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: quota_fraction at 1.0 and measured work at 0.15/0.015 may represent different quantities (configured quota ceiling versus observed work), so the constant quota value is not itself evidence of saturation; semantics are not defined in the evidence.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Confirm with the telemetry owner the definitions of quota_fraction versus cpu_work/db_work and which series are bound to the actual load path before interpreting the quota value.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment across the load generator, service, dependency, and telemetry sources before interpreting any timing relationship.
recommendations.rationale: resource-binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core and every correlation pair lists CLOCK_ALIGNMENT_UNKNOWN; without verified clocks the -1000ms peak lag cannot support a lead/lag ordering or a temporal causal hypothesis.

recommendations.action: Rerun with a varied load profile (steps or ramps in target rate) and a longer window so controls are no longer constant and the correlation headline selection can run.
recommendations.rationale: target_rate was constant at 60 req/s and was dropped as a constant control; associations 01–07 were not evaluable, and the two candidate associations (08–09) had headline selection UNAVAILABLE due to OBSERVATION_COUNT_UNSUPPORTED, so no family-corrected significance exists.

recommendations.action: Inspect generator and downstream telemetry/logs around epoch 1704067500000 to explain the active_threads increase (~3 to up to 6) and the downstream in_flight_requests growth, and document whether the step was intended test load.
recommendations.rationale: The only candidate anomaly is a p95 response step to a flat 100ms; if the increase is the intended workload step, the PASS verdict stands with no remediation needed; if unintended, it points to a configuration or load-path change to investigate. This is observability work, not a causal claim.

recommendations.action: Keep the current policy configuration; the PASS verdict does not require a rule change. If the 50ms→100ms shift matters operationally, configure a lower latency threshold and rerun so the product can evaluate it.
recommendations.rationale: The latency policy (p95 <= 200ms) PASSes both windows and the window policy summaries are PASS, so the verdict is PASS; only a rule the product evaluates can change that label, and NO_POLICY is not applicable here.

recommendations.action: Treat the response CANDIDATE anomaly as informational until confirmed by a rerun; before acting on it, note that the reference baseline has MAD 0 and the episode observed values are flat at 100ms.
recommendations.rationale: An episode detected against a zero-MAD flat reference is sensitive to any step and, combined with zero errors and zero queue depths, does not by itself demonstrate instability or user impact; the anomaly is a candidate, not a confirmed defect.

caveats: Candidate correlations association-08 and association-09 have uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED and no family-corrected significance; their headline selections are UNAVAILABLE with reason OBSERVATION_COUNT_UNSUPPORTED.
Clock alignment is not verified by core (clock_alignment not_verified_by_core), so timing-based ordering such as the -1000ms best lag is not interpretable as lead/lag.

Most correlation pairs were not evaluable (INSUFFICIENT_DATA) due to constant controls, no rank/residual variation, and resource delta below minimum; this is an analysis coverage limitation, not proof of stability or absence of a relationship.

The response anomaly was detected with a zero-MAD reference (reference_mad 0, reference_median 50) and the episode observed values are flat at 100ms; the reported step is sensitive to the flat baseline and does not prove degradation or user impact.
Zero errors, zero queue depths, and zero GC pause across the windows do not prove spare capacity, low load, or absence of a future problem.
Window denominators differ (reference 7200 samples vs workload-01 28800 samples); rates are consistent at ~60 req/s, but raw counts are not directly comparable across windows.
cpu-service-quota quota_fraction constant 1.0 is not interpreted as saturation or failure; its semantics relative to cpu_work/db_work are not defined in the evidence.
